# glinet_wifi_radio (Resource)

Manages the settings of a Wi-Fi radio of the router, for example `radio0`: channel, channel width, mode, transmit power, random BSSID and, for a 6 GHz radio, the PSC option. Use one instance of this resource for each radio. The radio always exists on the router, so create takes over the radio. Each attribute that is not set keeps the value of the router: the provider sends back the value that it reads from the router just before the write. The router carries the radio settings in the write of the main interface of the radio (`wifi.set_config`), as the web UI does. So the provider reads the SSID, the encryption, the hidden flag and the Wi-Fi password of the main interface from the router just before the write and sends them back unchanged; it does not manage them (see `glinet_wifi_interface`). When only `tx_power` changes, the provider sends `wifi.set_txpower` instead, as the web UI does. The provider sends a call only when one of its values differs: on create from the values of the router, on update from the state. A create whose values are equal to those of the router sends no write. The provider sends `channel` and `channel_width` only when one of them changes: the web UI does not send them while the Wi-Fi repeater uses the radio, and what the router does with them then is not known. The provider checks `mode`, `channel_width` and `channel` against the lists of the radio on the router before the write. The web UI also permits only the channels that fit the channel width; the provider does not check this, and what the router does with such a channel is not known. **Danger:** a write, for example a change of the channel or the channel width, can restart the Wi-Fi of the radio, which disconnects its clients; it is not known whether it also restarts the other radio. When the uplink of the router is a Wi-Fi repeater on the same radio, a write can cut the uplink, and a change of the channel or the channel width can make the repeater lose its access point. A write to the LAN configuration (`glinet_lan`) restarted the Wi-Fi of a GL-AXT1800 with firmware 4.7.0 and cut its repeater uplink until a reboot; a Wi-Fi write can probably do the same. The write of this resource was not tested on a router; the parameters come from the router's web UI. Destroy removes the resource from the Terraform state and does not change the router.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "glinet_wifi_radio" "radio5g" {
  name          = "radio0"
  channel       = 36
  channel_width = "80"
  tx_power      = "High"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Device name of the radio, for example `radio0` or `radio1` (`device` in the router API). Changing it replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `channel` (Number) Channel of the radio, or `0` for automatic (`channel` in the router API). The value must be one of the channels that the router lists for the radio. A DFS channel is permitted only when the router supports DFS (`dfs_support`), and a 6 GHz radio with `psc_channels_only` permits only PSC channels. When it is not set, the router value does not change.
- `channel_width` (String) Channel width in MHz, `20`, `40`, `80`, `160` or `320`, or `auto` (`htmode` in the router API). The router lists the largest width for each mode of the radio, and whether the radio supports `auto`; create and update fail when the value is not available for `mode`. When it is not set, the router value does not change.
- `mode` (String) Wi-Fi mode of the radio, for example `11a/n/ac/ax` (`hwmode` in the router API). The router lists the modes of each radio; create and update fail when the radio does not support the value. When it is not set, the router value does not change.
- `psc_channels_only` (Boolean) Whether a 6 GHz radio uses only the preferred scanning channels (PSC) (`chan_6g_only_psc` in the router API). Only for a radio with the band `6G`: create and update fail when it is set for another radio, and it is always null there. When it is `true`, `channel` must be `0` or a PSC channel; the web UI then sets a channel that is not a PSC channel to `0`, but the provider fails instead. The option is in the web UI code of firmware 4.8.3 and was not seen on a router. When it is not set, the router value does not change.
- `random_bssid` (Boolean) Whether the radio uses a random BSSID (`random_bssid` in the router API). When it is not set, the router value does not change.
- `tx_power` (String) Transmit power: `Max`, `High`, `Medium` or `Low` (`txpower` in the router API). When it is not set, the router value does not change.

### Read-Only

- `band` (String) Band of the radio, for example `5G`, `2G` or `6G` (`band` in the router API).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import ID is the device name of the Wi-Fi radio on the router.
terraform import glinet_wifi_radio.radio5g radio0
```
